content:
- Overestimate prices in the short term after positive sentiment spikes; model tends to overshoot early in the forecast horizon.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is weak or negative; model fails to capture downward momentum unless sentiment turns sharply bullish.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in the 30-day forecast (days 1–7) and underpredicts late (days 24–30), suggesting a lag in capturing trend reversals.
- When sentiment is high (e.g., >0.4), model often overreacts with sharp upward moves, but true price action tends to be more gradual or even reverses after peak.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized — model holds high prices longer than observed, especially after spikes; true price often corrects faster than forecast.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent bias toward higher prices when sentiment is volatile or mixed; model struggles to adjust for sentiment-driven volatility.
- If sentiment drops below 0.2, model often fails to reduce forecast significantly, leading to overestimation of price stability.
- Model tends to ignore sentiment decay in the final 7–10 days of forecast, leading to persistent overestimation of price stability or upward bias.
